prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.

worlds.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. Its records begin in 1520, when a family of cattle dealers took it over, and nearly every later entry is a fine, a flogging, or a jailing for grazing out of turn, carried out by the president's hired men. Villagers' petitions to the duke complain that no one had been punished for such things in their grandfathers' time, and the duke replied that the valley lay outside his rule. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
worlds.explanation: Nearly every entry is a punishment carried out by hired men, so the council's authority was "coercive." "Customary" fails because such punishments were unknown in the villagers' grandfathers' time. "Diffuse" fails because a single family and its president held power, and "ancillary" fails because the duke disclaimed any rule over the valley.

customary.why: Rule unknown to earlier generations is not grounded in custom.

diffuse.why: Power concentrated in one family and its president is not spread out.

ancillary.quote: the valley lay outside his rule
ancillary.why: With no higher authority over it, the council was not subordinate.

worlds.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. No charter or lord ever granted its powers, and its records contain no fines or punishments of any kind. Each spring the five eldest heads of household set the grazing turns, and for three centuries the entries justify every ruling in the same words, "as it was done in our fathers' time," while villagers who grazed out of turn are recorded as moving their herds when told. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
worlds.explanation: With no grant of power and no punishments, villagers still obeyed rulings justified by what their fathers had done, so the council's authority was "customary." "Coercive" fails because the records hold no punishments. "Diffuse" fails because five elders decided, and "ancillary" fails because no charter or lord stood behind it.

coercive.quote: no fines or punishments of any kind
coercive.why: Obedience without any punishment does not rest on force.

diffuse.quote: the five eldest heads of household
diffuse.why: Decisions lay with a fixed few, not spread out.

ancillary.quote: No charter or lord ever granted its powers
ancillary.why: Nothing above it granted or limited its power.

worlds.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. It had no president or permanent seat and answered to no lord; each spring whichever villagers came to the meeting voted the grazing turns, and enforcing them passed from village to village by the year, meaning only that the host village reminded anyone grazing out of turn. Its records lie scattered across a dozen parish chests in as many hands, and the rules in them shift from year to year with attendance. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
worlds.explanation: Decisions fell to whoever attended, enforcement rotated, and the records are scattered among a dozen parishes, so the council's authority was "diffuse." "Coercive" fails because enforcement was only a reminder. "Customary" fails because the rules shifted every year, and "ancillary" fails because it answered to no lord.

coercive.quote: reminded anyone grazing out of turn

customary.quote: shift from year to year with attendance
customary.why: Rules that change yearly are not grounded in long tradition.

ancillary.why: It was subordinate to no one.

worlds.passage: From the 1400s to the 1600s, a council governed the shared grazing lands of a remote mountain valley. A charter from the bishop's court in the town below created it in 1402, and its records are a steward's copies of the court's grazing orders, each followed by a note that it had been read out in the villages. Offenders appear in them only as names sent down to that court, whose judges set every fine. Surveying the valley's records, one historian characterized the council's authority over the villages as essentially ______.
worlds.explanation: The council copied and announced the court's orders and sent offenders to the court for judgment, so its authority was "ancillary" to the court's. "Coercive" fails because the court's judges, not the council, set the fines. "Customary" fails because a charter created it in 1402, and "diffuse" fails because a single steward kept its records.

coercive.why: The power to punish lay with the court, not the council.

customary.quote: A charter from the bishop's court
customary.why: Its powers came from a written grant, not custom.

diffuse.why: Its business ran through one officer.
